brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Three full bases at 0,0,0 / 1,0,0 / 2,0,0 in a straight line, joined with jointBolts and end caps

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:2,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain — full-depth drained bins with drainage holes
All three bins filled with soil and planted: basil-harvest, mint-harvest, parsley-harvest — visible from above and at 30° view

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell linear herb planter (0,0 - 1,0 - 2,0) with a full-depth drained bin in each cell, filled and planted with three herb varieties, joints locked and open faces capped; mesh check clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
